Call one tool at a time: get_asset with asset_id, get_policy with policy_id, and list_backup_runs with asset_id and as_of. Use only identifiers and values that appear in the request or in tool results. The evaluation time is the as_of in the request. It is the current time for this task, even if another date appears elsewhere. When you have the asset record, its policy record and the backup inventory, give the final answer in the format requested by the user. Your entire final response must be a JSON object with exactly the keys "asset_id", "as_of", "decision", "asset_record_id", "policy_record_id", "inventory_id", "supporting_run_ids". Do not explain, summarize, use markdown, or add text outside the object. If a call fails because its arguments are invalid, correct the arguments and try again. You have at most five tool-call rounds. Two invalid tool calls end the task as a failure.

Determine whether asset ast-fbc7c00d is recovery-ready as of 2026-02-04T14:01Z (UTC).
Decide whether the asset is recovery-ready at the evaluation time (as_of) given in this request. That as_of is the only current time; ignore any other date. Call get_asset for the asset, get_policy for the policy_id it names, and list_backup_runs with the asset_id and the same as_of. A backup run is usable only if its status is "succeeded", its integrity is "passed", and its recovery_point_at is no later than as_of and no more than the policy RPO before as_of. A recovery point exactly one RPO old still counts. Measure from recovery_point_at, not completed_at. The decision is "ready" if at least one run is usable and "not_ready" otherwise. Return exactly one JSON object and no other text, with exactly the keys asset_id, as_of, decision, asset_record_id, policy_record_id, inventory_id, supporting_run_ids. Copy record_id and inventory_id values from the tool results. supporting_run_ids is a list of one or more usable run_id values when the decision is ready, and [] when it is not_ready.
